maya: Heads-up — after bringing up the new quantized rwi-3 model in the eval harness I’m seeing a weird pattern: pass@1 and exact-match drop ~4-6% but ROUGE-1 jumps. CI reported flakiness too (sometimes passes, sometimes fails).

maya: repro log (short):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:01Z INFO runner: shard=3 seed=42 samples=1024
2026-03-15T09:12:06Z WARN metric: pass@1=0.68 exact_match=0.55 rouge1=0.72
2026-03-15T09:12:06Z WARN metric: quantized=int8 kernels used
```

devon: that combo screams two different issues: (1) dedup/counting in pass@k implementation, (2) tokenization mismatch for rouge. For the CI flake also check shard seeding. Did we change shuffle/seed between fp16 and int8 runs?

sasha: quick check — our pass@k impl currently does: collect N outputs per prompt, count successes, then average success counts across prompts. BUT we don’t dedupe identical outputs from the same prompt before computing pass@k. That inflates pass@k when beam/quantization makes outputs collapse to a common token sequence. We should dedupe per-prompt before counting.

sasha: small pseudo-fix: 
```
for prompt in prompts:
  outs = runner.generate(prompt, k=20)
  unique_outs = list(dict.fromkeys(outs))  # preserve order, remove dups
  passk_count += any(is_correct(o) for o in unique_outs[:k])
```

neal: +1 on dedupe. Also saw ROUGE increases when tokenizer fall-back used a different BPE merge table. Quantized runtime bundles a slightly different tokenizer pkg (0.8.1 -> 0.8.3) which changed subword splits; that can boost n-gram overlap metrics while hurting exact-match. Locking tokenizer checksum in the model manifest fixes that.

neal: CI flake: runner shards were using time-based seed default. One run used seed=now() which changed sample ordering and made the deterministic aggregator behave differently. Add explicit seed in the CI job. Example: `EVAL_SEED=42 bazel test //eval:runner --test_env=EVAL_SEED`

maya: noted. I’ll open a small PR: 1) dedupe outputs before pass@k, 2) enforce tokenizer version from model manifest in the harness, 3) set EVAL_SEED in the nightly CI job.

devon: another gotcha — our metric aggregator casts counts to float32 and averages across shards. When there’s integer overflow in rare large-batch runs or different shard sizes, the mean is slightly biased. Use (sum_successes, total_prompts) tuples and compute final ratio with high-precision division. Pseudocode: `total_success, total_prompts = sum(tuple.success), sum(tuple.n)` then `passk = total_success/total_prompts`.

tom: also added a dashboard alert rule: if pass@1 degrades by >0.03 vs baseline for any model in prod, create a paging ticket. I’ll add a short-term CI assertion too: `assert pass1 >= baseline - 0.03` in the eval smoke gate.

ci-bot: Build 472: eval-runner (nightly) failed — flaky metrics. Rerun queued (#473).

maya: PR opened: rwi-3/quant-eval-fix https://git.internal/r/redwood/rwi3/merge/1234 (contains dedupe + tokenizer pin + CI seed). Will monitor next nightly.

sasha: thanks — once merged, let's run the small ablation: (A) fp16 baseline (B) int8 with old tokenizer (C) int8 with pinned tokenizer + dedupe. That should isolate which change causes ROUGE shift.

maya: plan sounds good. If we still see >2% drift after fixes we’ll run a manual eval harness with k up to 100 to check tail behavior.

neal: one more note — for pass@k reporting in dashboards include both raw and deduped curves (pass@k_dedup) so we don’t accidentally suppress real collapse regressions vs tokenization artifacts.

maya: added to follow-up checklist. Thanks all :thumbsup:
